ZONDO JUSTICE – THE COUNTDOWN

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
With the first volume of the Zondo Commission’s Findings released – we asked what’s the next step in an exclusive sitdown interview with the Minister of Justice.

Unique Selling Point:
** JUSTICE MINISTER RONALD LAMOLA SIT DOWN INTERVIEW
** STAYING RELEVANT WITH ZONDO COMMISSION - IT WILL SHAPE THE FUTURE OF SOUTH AFRICA AND IS IMPORTANT FOR CB TO COVER IT FROM TIME TO TIME TO GIVE CONTEXT TO BIG NEWS STORY THAT IS NOT GOING ANY WHERE

Summary:
3 years and close to R1 billion rand of tax-payers money later South Africans have been shocked, outraged and frustrated by the revelations of grand corruptions exposed during the Zondo Commission testimonies.

But now what? What happens next? And more importantly when will the facilitators that looted for their own benefit at the expense of the nation be in orange overalls and behind bars?

We look at the way forward and ask if the NPA is capable of the securing prosecutions and finally delivery justice.


Further information:
Justice Minister Ronald Lamola has been outspoken about the extension and cost of the Zondo Commission – now the question begs with the findings how will he ensure that South Africans get the return on investment they deserve and that the whistleblowers that bravely spoke out are not taken for granted.

The final report will be released by August / September this year.

FAR FROM OVER
National Director of Public Prosecutions Shamila Batohi also told the committee investigators are processing evidence from the state capture inquiry before it starts prosecuting…

"As we all know there’s no cross-examination, well limited cross-examination, before the commission and so as the investigators, we have to anticipate those things and there’s a lot more work that needs to go into the investigation after we receive evidence from the commission."

Questions arise over the capability of the NPA, why investigations did not run concurrently and whether or not these delays will negatively impact the likelihood of whistleblowers turning witnesses.

ZONDO DEFENDS COSTS
Zondo confirmed the R1-billion cost this is roughly equal to the R864-million which McKinsey has repaid to Eskom and SAA after negotiations with his commission. That’s just one example. (I don’t others yet – but I’m sure I’ll find them)

“(Ultimately), the commission’s work can’t be measured in rands and cents,” Zondo said, adding that it had to be measured by a more substantive outcome. “(We have) to make sure looting doesn’t happen again. If the looting repeats itself, it would be a serious indictment on us as a country.”

It can’t be argued that South Africa’s effort to get under the skin of State Capture and seek ways to end it, is unprecedented. It deserves to go full circle and end with those that betrayed the country in order to line their own pockets see the inside of prison cells.

The evidence is there, the whistleblowers have stood up and pointed to the corruptors – the ball is now in the court of the South African justice system.

THE FOCUS
= WHAT’s NEXT?
= WITH KEY INSTITUTIONS COMPROMISED OVER THE YEARS – HOW DO WE GAURANTEE RESULTS
= HOW DO WE PROTECT THE EVIDENCE AND THE WITNESSES
= IS THE NPA CAPABLE? WHY NOT SOONER?

INTERVIEWS
 MINISTER RONALD LAMOLA – we do a short, focussed interview him, 10-15 questions – we don’t want to waste his time asking elements that won’t make the cut – we think it will appreciated that we are mindful of his time.
 PROF. MOLLIE PAINTER – GIBS Centre for Business Ethics – on the way forward – how we have this evidence and it needs to used responsibly.
 NEW COMMENTS FROM THEMBA MASEKO – unused comments that relate specific to the NPA and delayed justice.
 NEW COMMENTS FROM ATHOL WILLIAMS- – unused comments that relate specific to the NPA and delayed justice.
 NPA – we’ve requested an interview with the NPA – we worry that the minister will direct answers to the NPA and don’t want to leave that gap. I am waiting for confirmation.

** NO RECAP FROM THIS WEEK’s PIECE ON WHISTLEBLOWERS – AND NO RE-USING OF COMMENTS – THIS WILL BE NEW.
** BOTH ATHOL & THEMBA SPOKE WELL – CAN USE THEM JUST TO CUSHION THE NEW INTERVIEWS – DON’T WANT TO WASTE STRONG NEW INTERVIEWS LIKE THE SARS SAGA & JOHAN VAN LOGGENBERG AND THEN SAA & MATHULWANE MPSHE
** POSSIBILITY OF A PART 3 – IT CAN BE IN A FEW WEEKS IF YOU WANT IT – WHERE ARE THE FACILITATORS NOW – AND THEN WE INTERVIEW JVL &. MPSHE – GIVING THEIR STORIES THE TIME IT DESERVES – THE FACILITATORS IN THEIR STORIES ARE GREAT ROGUES THAT WE HAVE SO MUCH MATERIAL ON 

TREATMENT
Similar to the style of the Whistleblower piece, beautifully shot interviews – the b-roll visuals will be more focused on courts, jail, justice – still stylised. The feel will be more like a news piece though, will use some Zondo footage as well. I intend on using quite a bit of the Minister’s interview and hopefully the NPA – we don’t often get them.

EXTRA BUDGET
We’ll need to get some Zondo Commission Footage and possibly some stock stills.

STRUCTURE: JUSTICE – THE COUNTDOWN

VO: It’s not often that you get one-on-one interviews with the Minister of Justice and the National Director of Public Prosecutions.

Their mandate is simple - ensure justice is served. But it’s often easier said than done.

Last week we introduced you to three people who were fundamental in the fight back against state capture.

THABISO: History will record that not every South African was silent. //
ATHOL: we stood up publicly, we’ve pointed to where the bad people are//
THEMBA: did I do the right thing, would I do it again? //I don't have SHADOW OF A DOUBT that, I would do it again.

VO: Their courage to speak out, was just, the first step.

ATHOL: We've got some truth. We need that truth to be converted to justice.
THEMBA: The country can’t wait another 10 years for those who are responsible to be prosecuted. It has to happen NOW.

VO: Three years and close to R1 billion in taxpayer money later – the findings of the Zondo Commission of Inquiry into State Capture are finally being released. Whistleblowers have been vindicated.

LINK: WHAT WE HAVE ALL KNOWN ALREADY HAS BEEN CONFIRMED, AGAIN, UNPRECEDENTED GRAND CORRUPTION, STATE OWNED ENTITIES CAPTURED, THE FACILITATORS NAMED AND SHAMED

VO: The first two parts of the report have honed in on state capture henchmen, from government and the private sector - calling for criminal charges and prosecution.

The ball is now in the court of the South African justice system - it’s time to put those in charge, in the hot seat.

LINK: THE REPORT WAS SCATHING - IT HELD NO PUNCHES, PAINTING A PICTURE OF A COUNTRY ROBBED AND A BROKEN CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEM – RAISING QUESTIONS AROUND CAPACITY AND CAPABILITY.

NDPP: It's not just a scathing picture, it's the reality that the commission has actually sketched in the NPA.

VO: Advocate Shamila Batohi, admits the National Prosecuting Authority was decimated during the state capture years.

NDPP: For many years in South Africa, there was absolutely no will to bring these cases to court. In fact, there was a will to make sure that they never come to court.// I understand the frustrations of people in South Africa to see prosecutions faster, as a citizen of this country, I am frustrated. But as the national director, you must do something about it.

VO: But many may argue that the NPA is not doing enough about it.

The Gupta family is still at large, having fled to the United Arab Emirates in 2018. Their alleged looting amounts to a whopping R57 Billion - but the true cost to the state is estimated to be even higher.

Ronald Lamola is the Minister of Justice.

MASA: What's the plan of action to recover some of the funds that were looted from our country?
MINISTER: we are ready as the Department of Justice // to recover money in any jurisdictions
MASA: Does that mean any time soon we'll be seeing your teams flying across our borders and getting people who are involved like the Guptas?
MINISTER: There's a process of extradition, obviously, that is still being processed through the relevant channels//But I believe that extradition will happen at some point.

PROF: As a society,// just to see some of these people brought to justice would be so satisfying and would set a benchmark then for further successes.

VO: Professor Mollie Painter is from the GIBS Centre for Business Ethics. She says South Africans are tired of waiting.

PROF: Change, it starts one action at a time, so people can talk a lot. But at some point you just have to take the first step. Take the first action and follow on. M14

MASA: A criticism has been that you could have run these investigations concurrently with the commission.
NDPP: The Zondo Commission is a commission of inquiry, it does not investigate and to the standard that is required before one can bring criminal charges. And understand also that, you know, there's a lot of information in the commission that we will get full access to only when the work of the commission is completed

VO: The NPA has its work cut out with the findings of the Zondo Commission.

Part 1 lists at least 20 of the key orchestrators that drove the crippling looting of SAA and SARS - that list includes Dudu Myeni, Brian Molefe and Tom Moyane.

PArt 2 singles out Transnet as the primary site of State Capture in financial terms and focuses on Denel - a once highly regarded organisation that is now almost on its knees, unable to pay staff.

MASA: Do you think in our lifetime we will be seeing those who have been fingered in this report actually wearing orange overalls?
MINISTER: Definitely those that will be found guilty. They will definitely go to jail.

VO: The minister may sound somewhat optimistic, but to be fair, the Investigating Directorate has had some success on high profile corruption cases linked to state capture.

In October 2020, the first big arrests were made in the Bosasa Matter, the 2010 World Cup Police Accommodation Scandal and the Free State Asbestos DEal that centred around a R255-million audit of asbestos roofing.

Warrants have been issued for the Guptas, and at least three of their associates have been arrested and charged. But frustratingly, there is still a long list of government cronies who have been implicated but not yet seen a day in court.

MASA: do you concede that at some point there was a failure in the justice system?
MINISTER: Yes, that's what the report is saying, I mean,
MASA: It even says that there's a death of prosecutions. The NPA is the death of prosecution.
MINISTER: The report says that I mean, you can't argue with that. // There was no action. // the wheels of justice are turning. // there is also a turning point within the the the NPA and also the Hawks, //But is it enough is not enough..

VO: The Zondo Commission Reports have made clear recommendations on prosecutions, policy and changes to law. But it is important not to forget these recommendations are just that - recommendations.

LINK: // WE’VE BEEN DOWN THIS ROAD - COMMISSIONS OF ENQUIRIES HAVE COME AND GONE, THERE HAVE BEEN SOME PROSECUTIONS, AND SOME DEGREE OF ACCOUNTABILITY …. different

NDPP: Perhaps what's different is that our country is on a knife edge, // quick, effective, impactful prosecutions. Critical to pulling us back from the edge. // M24
MASA: How positive are you that you will see successful prosecutions coming out of the Zondo Commisison.
NDPP: /I'm hoping, in fact, that in the next month, there will be at least one really good case. And hopefully, you know, at best, maybe three. / I accept that there's a huge credibility and trust deficit. But all I want to say to South Africans is look at where we've come from.

VO: With many of the main orchestrators of state capture not yet behind bars, the country’s patience is running thin and the pressure is on for the NPA to deliver watertight cases.

NDPP: //building these cases is not easy. They do take time and failure is not an option. //. That said, there will be cases that we will lose.
MASA: So not everybody is going to get prosecuted. Some are going to get away scot free.
NDPP: I think that's the reality. //We follow the evidence and where the evidence takes us, we will prosecute people. We will certainly, in our strategies, aim to do to bring to court or to prosecute those most responsible for state capture. //But at the end of the day, whether everyone is prosecuted. I can't SAY.

VO: And some of those that stand accused of corruption, shamelessly try to use the law to their advantage in an attempt to evade justice.

PROF: law is a double edged sword. It can be used to // protect both the innocent and protect organizations or individuals with a lot of power//

VO: Minister Lamalo says his department’s mandate is clear.

MINISTER: the courts must adjudicate. Decisions must be made. The NPA must act without any fear or favour, irrespective of who they are prosecuting. That is what the law is.

VO: It’s a balancing act between the rights of the accused and the rights of the victims with the interest of justice.

NDPP: we've even been looking at at a very, very robust and strong litigation strategy to counter these strategies of defence.// it has to be more difficult for accused persons to simply delay and delay without consequences

VO: The ZOndo Commission has also made it clear that new strategies need to be implemented to protect whistleblowers.

Both Themba Maseko and Athol Williams have been on the receiving end of harassment and threats aimed at silenc them.

THEMBA: If they intimidate and do the worst whistle blowers, they are hoping that in fact, the courts, the cases will not succeed in court
ATHOL: We are playing into the hands of the corrupt // we will lose our fight against corruption and state capture. If we do not support and protect whistleblowers //

MASA: If whistleblowers stop coming forward, what does that do for your job?
NDPP: the impact is devastating. //injustice flourishes when good people do nothing. And whistleblowers are good people //.

VO: But with threats against whistleblowers mounting, on it’s own, simply changing the law won’t cut it .

NDPP: how do we protect them now? And I think it's really important that that government, that civil society, that business really all come together to look at how we can we can provide support and assistance to whistleblowers..

PROF: // it's everybody's problem. And everybody should see themselves as the custodians of societal justice and freedom and the sanctity of of life and livelihoods.

VO: Advocate Batohi is confident that all is not lost.

NDPP: The days of impunity are no longer guaranteed. That it's not about if, but it's about when people will be held to account. // we are much better equipped to bring cases more quickly to court now to. // please don't lose trust in us.

VO: Time alone will tell, and the clock is ticking…

END


PROMO 1 – 10 SECONDS
VO: With the first two parts of the Zondo Commission’s Findings released – we ask when the country can expect justice in rare sit-down interviews with the Minister of Justice and the National Director of Public Prosecutions.


PROMO 2 - 21 seconds
VO: 3 years and close to R1 billion rand of tax-payers money later, the Zondo Commission is releasing the inquiry’s findings on grand corruptions and state capture.

ATHOL: We've got some truth. We need that truth to be converted to justice.

VO: We ask what happens next?


PROMO 3 - 21 seconds
VO: THE FIRST TWO PARTS OF THE ZONDO COMMISSION’S FINDINGS WERE SCATHING - IT PAINTS A PICTURE OF A COUNTRY ROBBED AND A BROKEN CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEM.

NDPP: It's not just a scathing picture, it's the reality that the commission has actually sketched in the NPA.

VO: But is the NPA now ready and capable of the securing prosecutions and finally delivery justice.

MINISTER: The report says that I mean, you can't argue with that. // There was no action. // the wheels of justice are turning. // there is also a turning point within the the the NPA and also the Hawks, //But is it enough is not enough.. VO: The Zondo Commission Reports have made clear recommendations on prosecutions, policy and changes to law. But it is important not to forget these recommendations are just that - recommendations. LINK: // WE’VE BEEN DOWN THIS ROAD - COMMISSIONS OF ENQUIRIES HAVE COME AND GONE, THERE HAVE BEEN SOME PROSECUTIONS, AND SOME DEGREE OF ACCOUNTABILITY …. different NDPP: Perhaps what's different is that our country is on a knife edge, // quick, effective, impactful prosecutions. Critical to pulling us back from the edge. // M24 MASA: How positive are you that you will see successful prosecutions coming out of the Zondo Commisison. NDPP: /I'm hoping, in fact, that in the next month, there will be at least one really good case. And hopefully, you know, at best, maybe three. / I accept that there's a huge credibility and trust deficit. But all I want to say to South Africans is look at where we've come from. VO: With many of the main orchestrators of state capture not yet behind bars, the country’s patience is running thin and the pressure is on for the NPA to deliver watertight cases. NDPP: //building these cases is not easy. They do take time and failure is not an option. //. That said, there will be cases that we will lose. MASA: So not everybody is going to get prosecuted. Some are going to get away scot free. NDPP: I think that's the reality. //We follow the evidence and where the evidence takes us, we will prosecute people. We will certainly, in our strategies, aim to do to bring to court or to prosecute those most responsible for state capture. //But at the end of the day, whether everyone is prosecuted. I can't SAY. VO: And some of those that stand accused of corruption, shamelessly try to use the law to their advantage in an attempt to evade justice. PROF: law is a double edged sword. It can be used to // protect both the innocent and protect organizations or individuals with a lot of power// VO: Minister Lamalo says his department’s mandate is clear. MINISTER: the courts must adjudicate. Decisions must be made. The NPA must act without any fear or favour, irrespective of who they are prosecuting. That is what the law is. VO: It’s a balancing act between the rights of the accused and the rights of the victims with the interest of justice. NDPP: we've even been looking at at a very, very robust and strong litigation strategy to counter these strategies of defence.// it has to be more difficult for accused persons to simply delay and delay without consequences VO: The ZOndo Commission has also made it clear that new strategies need to be implemented to protect whistleblowers. Both Themba Maseko and Athol Williams have been on the receiving end of harassment and threats aimed at silenc them. THEMBA: If they intimidate and do the worst whistle blowers, they are hoping that in fact, the courts, the cases will not succeed in court ATHOL: We are playing into the hands of the corrupt // we will lose our fight against corruption and state capture. If we do not support and protect whistleblowers // MASA: If whistleblowers stop coming forward, what does that do for your job? NDPP: the impact is devastating. //injustice flourishes when good people do nothing. And whistleblowers are good people //. VO: But with threats against whistleblowers mounting, on it’s own, simply changing the law won’t cut it . NDPP: how do we protect them now? And I think it's really important that that government, that civil society, that business really all come together to look at how we can we can provide support and assistance to whistleblowers.. PROF: // it's everybody's problem. And everybody should see themselves as the custodians of societal justice and freedom and the sanctity of of life and livelihoods. That it's not about if, but it's about when people will be held to account. // we are much better equipped to bring cases more quickly to court now to. // please don't lose trust in us. metadata.Unique Selling Point: ** JUSTICE MINISTER RONALD LAMOLA SIT DOWN INTERVIEW ** STAYING RELEVANT WITH ZONDO COMMISSION - IT WILL SHAPE THE FUTURE OF SOUTH AFRICA AND IS IMPORTANT FOR CB TO COVER IT FROM TIME TO TIME TO GIVE CONTEXT TO BIG NEWS STORY THAT IS NOT GOING ANY WHERE
metadata.Summary: 3 years and close to R1 billion rand of tax-payers money later South Africans have been shocked, outraged and frustrated by the revelations of grand corruptions exposed during the Zondo Commission testimonies. But now what? What happens next? And more importantly when will the facilitators that looted for their own benefit at the expense of the nation be in orange overalls and behind bars? We look at the way forward and ask if the NPA is capable of the securing prosecutions and finally delivery justice.
metadata.Further information: Justice Minister Ronald Lamola has been outspoken about the extension and cost of the Zondo Commission – now the question begs with the findings how will he ensure that South Africans get the return on investment they deserve and that the whistleblowers that bravely spoke out are not taken for granted. The final report will be released by August / September this year. FAR FROM OVER National Director of Public Prosecutions Shamila Batohi also told the committee investigators are processing evidence from the state capture inquiry before it starts prosecuting… "As we all know there’s no cross-examination, well limited cross-examination, before the commission and so as the investigators, we have to anticipate those things and there’s a lot more work that needs to go into the investigation after we receive evidence from the commission." Questions arise over the capability of the NPA, why investigations did not run concurrently and whether or not these delays will negatively impact the likelihood of whistleblowers turning witnesses. ZONDO DEFENDS COSTS Zondo confirmed the R1-billion cost this is roughly equal to the R864-million which McKinsey has repaid to Eskom and SAA after negotiations with his commission. That’s just one example. (I don’t others yet – but I’m sure I’ll find them) “(Ultimately), the commission’s work can’t be measured in rands and cents,” Zondo said, adding that it had to be measured by a more substantive outcome. “(We have) to make sure looting doesn’t happen again. If the looting repeats itself, it would be a serious indictment on us as a country.” It can’t be argued that South Africa’s effort to get under the skin of State Capture and seek ways to end it, is unprecedented. It deserves to go full circle and end with those that betrayed the country in order to line their own pockets see the inside of prison cells. The evidence is there, the whistleblowers have stood up and pointed to the corruptors – the ball is now in the court of the South African justice system. THE FOCUS = WHAT’s NEXT? = WITH KEY INSTITUTIONS COMPROMISED OVER THE YEARS – HOW DO WE GAURANTEE RESULTS = HOW DO WE PROTECT THE EVIDENCE AND THE WITNESSES = IS THE NPA CAPABLE? WHY NOT SOONER?
